llm.summary: This skill is presented as a terminal notification manager, but the shipped script mainly stores arbitrary command inputs in local log files and does not implement the advertised scheduling, alert delivery, filtering, or delivery tracking.

dimensions.detail: The script works offline and writes only under ~/.local/share/notification, which is bounded, but it retains raw user-provided content and export behavior is confusing because duplicate case labels make the documented export/status functions unreachable.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact includes an executable shell script but no separate installer or dependency setup was present in the inspected files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Several commands are generic and underdefined, and the documentation includes pseudo-output and shell-like fragments that do not clearly describe safe inputs, outputs, or side effects.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: User input is persistently written in plaintext to per-command logs and history.log without explicit permission hardening, retention controls, or deletion controls; this is partly disclosed as local history but still under-scoped for notification contents.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The manifest claims notification scheduling, filtering, sending alerts, and delivery tracking, while the script implements a generic local logger/search/history interface and has no notification dispatch or scheduling logic.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this carefully before installing. It should not be relied on for real alerts, scheduled notifications, filtering, or delivery confirmation. Treat it as a local plaintext logging utility, avoid entering secrets or sensitive notification content, and inspect or remove ~/.local/share/notification if you test it.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the artifact advertises notification operations that the script does not perform, creating a material mismatch for agents or users relying on alerts.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted in substance: both the help text and command handlers show generic logging behavior rather than notification scheduling, delivery, filtering, or confirmation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted in substance: command names and documentation are too vague to establish reliable operational boundaries.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in substance but not treated as malicious: comments and branding call it a notification utility, while implemented behavior is a logging utility.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted in substance: convert, analyze, generate, batch, compare, report, and config are not coherently tied to notification management.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted: local history/export is disclosed as a feature, but raw plaintext retention lacks clear controls and restrictive permission handling.
[T09] expected: Accepted as a contextual risk: plaintext local storage is consistent with the local-history design, but permissions depend on the user's environment and sensitive content may be exposed on shared systems.
